verses.33:44: They departed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, at the border of Moab.
verses.33:45: They departed from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
verses.33:46: They departed from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
verses.33:47: They departed from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
verses.33:48: They departed from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
verses.33:49: They camped along the Jordan, from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
verses.33:50: Then the LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
verses.33:51: "Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When you cross over the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.33:52: then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, destroy all their figured images, destroy all their cast images, and demolish all their high places.
verses.33:53: And you shall take possession of the land and dwell in it, for to you I have given the land to possess it.
verses.33:54: You shall take the land as an inheritance by lot according to your clans: to a larger one you shall increase its inheritance, and to a smaller one you shall reduce its inheritance. Wherever the lot comes out for each one, it shall belong to him; according to the tribes of your fathers you shall take your inheritance.
verses.33:55: But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those of them whom you leave remaining will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the land in which you dwell.
verses.33:56: And it will happen that just as I intended to do to them, I will do to you.'"
verses.34:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:2: "Command the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When you come into the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan by its boundaries.
verses.34:3: Your southern side shall be from the wilderness of Zin beside Edom, and your southern boundary shall be from the edge of the Salt Sea eastward.
verses.34:4: Then the boundary shall turn for you south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass on to Zin, and its outer limits shall be south of Kadesh-barnea; then it shall go out to Hazar-addar and pass on to Azmon.
verses.34:5: And the boundary shall turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt, and its outer limits shall be at the sea.
verses.34:6: For the western boundary, the Great Sea and its border shall be yours; this shall be your western boundary.
verses.34:7: And this shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line to Mount Hor.
verses.34:8: From Mount Hor you shall mark out a line to Lebo-hamath, and the outer limits of the boundary shall be at Zedad.
verses.34:9: Then the boundary shall go out to Ziphron, and its outer limits shall be at Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
verses.34:10: And you shall mark out for yourselves the eastern boundary from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
verses.34:11: The boundary shall go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; then the boundary shall go down and reach the slope of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east.
verses.34:12: And the boundary shall go down to the Jordan, and its outer limits shall be at the Salt Sea. This shall be the land for you by its boundaries all around.'"
verses.34:13: Then Moses commanded the sons of Israel, saying, "This is the land that you shall inherit for yourselves by lot, which the LORD has commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
verses.34:14: For the tribe of the sons of the Reubenites according to their fathers' households and the tribe of the sons of the Gadites according to their fathers' households have taken their inheritance, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has taken its inheritance.
verses.34:15: The two tribes and the half-tribe have taken their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward toward the sunrise."
verses.34:16: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.34:17: "These are the names of the men who shall apportion the land for you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
verses.34:18: And you shall take one leader from each tribe to apportion the land as an inheritance.
verses.34:19: And these are the names of the men: for the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
verses.34:20: And for the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud.
verses.34:21: For the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon.
verses.34:22: And for the tribe of the sons of Dan, a leader, Bukki son of Jogli.
verses.34:23: For the sons of Joseph: for the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod.
verses.34:24: And for the tribe of the sons of Ephraim, a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
verses.34:25: And for the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
verses.34:26: And for the tribe of the sons of Issachar, a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan.
verses.34:27: And for the tribe of the sons of Asher, a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
verses.34:28: And for the tribe of the sons of Naphtali, a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud."
verses.34:29: These are the ones whom the LORD commanded to apportion the inheritance to the sons of Israel in the land of Canaan.
verses.35:1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
verses.35:2: "Command the sons of Israel that they give to the Levites, from the inheritance of their possession, cities to live in; and you shall give to the Levites pastureland for the cities all around them.
verses.35:3: The cities shall be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands shall be for their livestock, for their property, and for all their animals.
verses.35:4: The pasturelands of the cities that you give to the Levites shall reach from the wall of the city outward a thousand cubits all around.
verses.35:5: And you shall measure outside the city on the east side two thousand cubits, and on the south side two thousand cubits, and on the west side two thousand cubits, and on the north side two thousand cubits, with the city in the middle. This shall be theirs as the pasturelands of the cities.
verses.35:6: The cities that you give to the Levites shall be the six cities of refuge, which you shall give so that the killer may flee there, and in addition to them you shall give forty-two cities.
verses.35:7: All the cities that you give to the Levites shall be forty-eight cities, both them and their pasturelands.
verses.35:8: And as for the cities that you give from the possession of the sons of Israel, from the larger you shall take more and from the smaller you shall take fewer; each one, in proportion to his inheritance that they inherit, shall give from his cities to the Levites."
verses.35:9: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.35:10: "Speak to the sons of Israel and say to them, 'When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
verses.35:11: then you shall designate for yourselves cities that shall be cities of refuge for you, so that a killer who strikes down a person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.35:12: The cities shall be a refuge for you from the avenger, so that the killer will not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
verses.35:13: And the cities that you give shall be six cities of refuge for you.
verses.35:14: Three of the cities you shall give beyond the Jordan, and three of the cities you shall give in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
verses.35:15: For the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner and for the temporary resident among them, these six cities shall be a refuge, so that anyone who strikes down a person unintentionally may flee there.
verses.35:16: But if he struck him with an iron object and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:17: And if he struck him with a stone in the hand by which one might die, and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:18: Or if he struck him with a wooden object in the hand by which one might die, and he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:19: The avenger of blood himself shall put the murderer to death; when he meets him, he himself shall put him to death.
verses.35:20: And if in hatred he pushed him, or threw something at him while lying in wait, and he died,
verses.35:21: or in enmity struck him with his hand, and he died, the one who struck him shall surely be put to death; he is a murderer. The avenger of blood shall put the murderer to death when he meets him.
verses.35:22: But if suddenly, without enmity, he pushed him, or threw any object at him without lying in wait,
verses.35:23: or without seeing dropped on him any stone by which one might die, and he died, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking his harm,
verses.35:24: then the congregation shall judge between the one who struck him and the avenger of blood according to these judgments.
verses.35:25: And the congregation shall rescue the killer from the hand of the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall return him to his city of refuge to which he had fled; and he shall live in it until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
verses.35:26: But if the killer ever goes outside the boundary of his city of refuge to which he flees,
verses.35:27: and the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundary of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the killer, there shall be no bloodguilt on him.
verses.35:28: For he must live in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; but after the death of the high priest, the killer may return to the land of his possession.
verses.35:29: And these things shall be for you a statute of judgment throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
verses.35:30: If anyone strikes down a person, the murderer shall be put to death on the testimony of witnesses; but one witness shall not testify against a person so that he dies.
verses.35:31: And you shall not take a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death, for he shall surely be put to death.
verses.35:32: And you shall not take a ransom for one who has fled to his city of refuge, so that he might return to live in the land before the death of the priest.
verses.35:33: You shall not pollute the land where you are, for blood is what pollutes the land; and for the land, atonement cannot be made for the blood shed in it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
verses.35:34: And you shall not defile the land where you are living, in whose midst I dwell; for I, the LORD, dwell among the sons of Israel.'"
verses.36:1: Then the heads of the fathers' houses belonging to the clan of the sons of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from among the clans of the sons of Joseph, approached and spoke before Moses and before the chieftains, the heads of the fathers' houses of the sons of Israel.
verses.36:2: They said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land as an inheritance by lot to the sons of Israel, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give our brother Zelophehad's inheritance to his daughters.
verses.36:3: Now if they become wives to any of the sons of the tribes of the sons of Israel, then their inheritance will be deducted from the inheritance of our fathers and will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they will belong; and it will be deducted from the lot of our inheritance.
verses.36:4: And when the jubilee comes for the sons of Israel, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they will belong, and their inheritance will be deducted from the inheritance of our fathers' tribe."
verses.36:5: Then Moses commanded the sons of Israel at the word of the LORD, saying, "The tribe of the sons of Joseph is speaking rightly.
verses.36:6: This is the matter that the LORD has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, 'Let them become wives to whoever is good in their eyes; only they must become wives within the clan of their father's tribe.
verses.36:7: And no inheritance belonging to the sons of Israel shall pass from tribe to tribe, for each of the sons of Israel shall cling to the inheritance of his fathers' tribe.
verses.36:8: And every daughter who possesses an inheritance from the tribes of the sons of Israel shall become a wife to one from the clan of her father's tribe, so that each of the sons of Israel may possess the inheritance of his fathers.
verses.36:9: And no inheritance shall pass from one tribe to another tribe, for each of the tribes of the sons of Israel shall cling to its inheritance.'"
verses.36:10: As the LORD commanded Moses, so the daughters of Zelophehad did.
verses.36:11: Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, became wives to the sons of their uncles.
verses.36:12: They became wives within the clans of the sons of Manasseh, son of Joseph, and their inheritance stayed with the tribe of their father's clan.
verses.36:13: These are the commandments and the judgments that the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to the sons of Israel on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan at Jericho.

notes.1:2: Hebrew se'u et-ro'sh literally means "lift up the head of," an idiom for taking a tally or census (also in 1:49). Likewise, legulgelotam literally means "according to their skulls," denoting an individual headcount.
notes.1:16: Ketiv qry'y (adjectival qatil plural construct, "chosen/called ones of") vs. Qere qeru'e (Qal passive participle plural construct of qara', "those summoned of"); translated following the Qere. The noun 'alpe ("thousands") can also denote tribal military divisions or clans.
notes.1:18: The verb wayyityalledu ("and they declared their lineage") is a biblical hapax legomenon in the Hithpael stem of yalad ("bear/beget"), expressing reflexive declaration or enrollment of one's ancestry.
notes.1:47: The verb hotpaqedu ("were registered") is in the rare Hothpaal (passive reflexive) stem of paqad, contrasting with the Qal stem used throughout this chapter for official census registration and the Hiphil stem in 1:50 ("appoint").
notes.1:51: The substantivized Qal participle hazzar ("the outsider," from zur, "be a stranger") denotes any unauthorized non-Levite who approaches the tabernacle and its sacred service.
notes.2:2: Hebrew degel ("banner") denotes a tribal military standard and, by extension throughout this chapter, the three-tribe division grouped under it, paired here with the plural otot ("emblems") for the smaller insignia of each ancestral house. Hebrew minneged denotes a position facing opposite from a distance.
notes.2:6: Here and in verses 8 and 11, the Masoretic Text uses the third-person masculine singular suffix in pequdav ("his mustered men", referring to the leader or tribe), whereas the other nine tribal entries use the third-person masculine plural suffix in pequdehem ("their mustered men", referring to the sons of the tribe).
notes.2:14: The Masoretic Text reads Reuel here, whereas Numbers 1:14, 7:42, 7:47, and 10:20 read Deuel, reflecting the graphical similarity between Hebrew resh and dalet.
notes.2:17: "At his post" translates the Hebrew idiom al-yado (literally "at his hand"), denoting an appointed place or station. "The camp of the Levites" stands in direct apposition to "the tent of meeting" without a conjunction or preposition in the Hebrew.
notes.2:33: "Were ... mustered" renders the rare Hothpaal reflexive-passive form hotpaqdu (from paqad), attested in the Hebrew Bible only in Numbers 1:47, 2:33, 26:62, and 1 Kings 20:27.
notes.3:3: Hebrew mille yadam is literally 'he filled their hand' (Piel perfect of male, 'fill'), the standard priestly idiom for ordination or installation into office.
notes.3:7: The cognate verb-and-noun idiom shamar mishmeret (literally 'guard a guard-duty' or 'keep a charge') recurs throughout the chapter (vv. 7, 8, 28, 32, 38) for both protective vigilance over the sanctuary and assigned custodial duties.
notes.3:9: Hebrew netunim netunim is literally 'given, given' (a doubled Qal passive participle of natan, 'give'), using repetition to express complete dedication.
notes.3:39: The Masoretic Text places extraordinary points (puncta extraordinaria) above 'and Aaron,' an ancient scribal marker of textual doubt (cf. vv. 15-16). In addition, the MT total here is 22,000, whereas the clan figures in vv. 22, 28, and 34 (7,500 + 8,600 + 6,200) sum to 22,300.
notes.3:46: Hebrew peduyim (plural of the Qal passive participle of padah, 'redeem') functions as an abstract noun for 'redemption' or 'redemption price' in vv. 46, 48, and 51 (alongside pidyom in v. 49), whereas peduye halwiyyim in v. 49 concretely denotes 'those redeemed by the Levites.'
notes.4:2: Literally, "Lift up the head of" (using the Qal infinitive absolute imperatively), a Hebrew idiom for taking a census or headcount (also in 4:22).
notes.4:6: The Hebrew term tachash (also in 4:8, 10-12, 14, 25) is of uncertain meaning, referring either to fine tanned leather or to the hide of a marine animal such as a dugong or dolphin.
notes.4:13: The Hebrew verb dishshenu is a privative Piel of deshen ("fatty ashes"), literally "de-ash," meaning to clear away the ashes from the altar.
notes.4:20: Hebrew keballa (preposition ke- with the Piel infinitive construct of bala, "swallow up") literally means "as a swallowing," idiomatically "for an instant"; some alternatively construe it transitively with the following object as "while the sacred things are being covered" or "dismantled."
notes.4:49: The 3ms active verb paqad ("he registered") is used impersonally here for the passive ("they were registered"), and ufequdav is the Qal passive participle with a 3ms agentive suffix, literally "and those registered by him."
notes.5:2: Hebrew tsarua (Qal passive participle of tsara) denotes someone afflicted with the ritual skin condition traditionally called leprosy (tsara'at; cf. Lev 13-14), a broader category than modern Hansen's disease.
notes.5:7: Hebrew asham ("guilt") here concretely denotes the restitution owed for a wrong, and be-rosho (literally "in its head/principal") means the full principal amount.
notes.5:10: The Hebrew syntax is terse: et-qodashav ("his holy gifts") is marked by the particle et yet serves as the grammatical subject of the plural verb yihyu ("shall be"), leaving the referent of the first "his" (the donor or the priest) open to interpretation.
notes.5:18: Hebrew literally reads "loosen the head of the woman" (para et-rosh ha-ishshah), an idiom for unbinding her hair so it hangs loose (cf. Lev 10:6; 21:10).
notes.5:22: Both latsbot ("to make swell") and lanpil ("to make fall away") are syncopated Hiphil infinitives construct with elided he (for le-hatzbot and le-hanpil), with lanpil also retaining an unassimilated nun.
notes.6:2: Hebrew yafli (Hiphil of pala) means "makes an extraordinary/special [vow]" or "specifically vows"; the root nazar (Hiphil hizzir, noun nezer) means "separate/dedicate," underlying the term Nazirite (nazir) and used with min in v. 3 for "abstain from."
notes.6:4: Both chartzannim ("seeds") and zag ("skin") occur only here in the Hebrew Bible; while ancient interpreters debated which term referred to grape seeds and which to skins, together they forbid every part of the grape.
notes.6:13: Hebrew yavi oto (literally "he shall bring him") uses an impersonal third-person active verb with passive force, "he shall be brought."
notes.6:23: In the Hebrew the divine promise ("so they shall place My name on the sons of Israel, and I will bless them") stands as v. 27, after the blessing; this edition's verse order places it here at the end of v. 23, before the blessing.
notes.6:26: Hebrew repeats panav elekha ("His face toward you") in both vv. 25 and 26, and concludes with the jussive ve-yasem (from sim, "set/establish," echoing "place My name," v. 27 in the Hebrew) rather than natan ("give").
notes.7:3: The rare term tsav (occurring in this sense elsewhere only in Isa 66:20) denotes a covered transport wagon or litter-cart; rendering "covered wagons" follows ancient versions and standard Hebrew lexicography.
notes.7:10: "The dedication offering for the altar" renders Hebrew chanukkat hammizbeach, literally "the dedication of the altar," used metonymically for the gift marking its dedication. "On the day it was anointed" translates a Niphal infinitive construct (himmashach) whose patient takes the direct object marker (oto), a standard passive-infinitive construction in Biblical Hebrew.
notes.7:14: Literally "one cup, ten of gold." As with "one hundred thirty" in v. 13, the weight unit "shekels" is omitted by standard Hebrew idiom for weights (cf. Gen 24:22).
notes.7:18: On the second day the Masoretic Text uniquely repeats the Hiphil verb hiqriv ("presented," spelled defectively in v. 19), whereas the introductory entries from the third day onward (vv. 24, 30, 36, 42) omit the verb entirely in verbless ledger clauses.
notes.7:72: Literally "on day eleven day" (similarly v. 78, "on day twelve day"). Because Biblical Hebrew lacks ordinal adjectives above ten, it expresses "eleventh" and "twelfth" using the cardinal numeral framed by the repeated noun "day."
notes.7:86: Literally "ten, ten the cup," using Hebrew distributive repetition to indicate "ten shekels for each cup," with the weight unit "shekels" omitted by idiom here and in v. 85.
notes.7:89: "Speaking" renders the rare Hithpael participle middabber (with assimilated taw, cf. Ezek 2:2; 43:6), and "atonement cover" renders hakkapporet. The closing clause "and He spoke to him" (Piel wayyiqtol) takes God as subject, mirroring "with Him" earlier in the verse, though "the voice" is also grammatically possible ("and it spoke to him").
notes.8:2: The Hiphil infinitive construct of alah (literally "when you cause the lamps to go up") is the technical expression for setting up and lighting the lamps on the lampstand.
notes.8:11: The cognate phrase "wave as a wave offering" (Hiphil of nuph with tenuphah) denotes a ritual ceremony of presentation or elevation transferring the Levites into the service of the LORD.
notes.8:16: Hebrew emphatically repeats the Qal passive participle netunim ("given, given") to stress complete dedication, and uses the unique noun pitrat ("what opens," found only here) instead of the usual peter.
notes.8:21: "Cleansed themselves from sin" renders the privative Hithpael of chata (ritual decontamination from sin or impurity), distinct from the Piel of taher ("to purify them") at the end of the verse.
notes.8:24: "Serve a term of duty" renders the cognate idiom litzbo tzaba (Qal infinitive construct of tzaba with its noun), a military term extended here to the Levites' scheduled sanctuary duty.
notes.9:3: "At twilight" translates the Hebrew dual idiom beyn ha'arbayim (literally "between the two evenings"), referring to the interval between late afternoon or sunset and full darkness.
notes.9:6: "Because of a human corpse" renders lenephesh adam; in priestly legal contexts nephesh commonly denotes a dead body, in contrast to its sense "person" in 9:13.
notes.9:10: The Masoretic text places an extraordinary dot (punctum extraordinarium) over the final letter of rechoqah ("distant"), an ancient scribal mark indicating textual scrutiny or legal qualification.
notes.9:15: "Was raised up" translates the impersonal Hiphil infinitive construct haqim ("on the day of raising up the tabernacle"), and the preposition lamed on "the tent of the testimony" functions appositionally to specify the tabernacle.
notes.9:16: The Masoretic Hebrew omits "by day" (implied by contrast with "by night"), and verses 15b-23 employ habitual imperfect verbs to describe recurring past actions ("would cover," "would set out").
notes.10:21: "The sanctuary" (ha-miqdāš) refers metonymically to the sacred furnishings of the sanctuary carried by the Kohathites (cf. Num 4:15). The passive rendering "was set up" represents an impersonal third-person plural Hiphil (wəhēqîmû, literally "and they set up"), referring to the Gershonites and Merarites arriving ahead of them.
notes.10:34: In the Hebrew, the cloud verse is 10:34 and the Song of the Ark is 10:35-36; this edition's verse numbering places the Song of the Ark at 10:34-35 and the cloud verse at 10:36, the order also found in the Septuagint.
notes.10:35: The infinitive construct bənuḥōh ("when it came to rest") exhibits an archaic third-person masculine singular suffix (-ōh). The phrase "to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel" renders an unmarked directive accusative construct chain (riḇəḇōṯ ʾalpê yiśrāʾēl) following the imperative "Return."
notes.11:1: The participle kəmiṯʾōnənîm (Hithpolel of ʾnn, "acting like complainers") is rare, occurring elsewhere only in Lamentations 3:39. The noun raʿ ("hardship" or "evil") may be read either as the subject of their complaint or, following the Masoretic cantillation, as a predicate assessing it as "evil in the ears of the LORD."
notes.11:8: "Rich oil" translates ləšaḏ haššāmen (literally "the moisture/richness of oil"), using the rare noun ləšaḏ (elsewhere only in Psalm 32:4), which denotes fresh oil or an oil-rich delicacy.
notes.11:15: The second-person pronoun addressing God is unusually spelled as the short form ʾat (normally feminine singular) alongside the masculine singular participle ʿōśeh ("treating"), a rare Masoretic orthographic feature also attested in Deuteronomy 5 and Ezekiel 28.
notes.11:25: "But they did not do so again" translates wəlōʾ yāsāpû (Qal of ysp, "add/continue/repeat"), indicating that their ecstatic prophesying was a one-time sign; several ancient versions instead derived the verb from swp ("cease"), rendering "and did not cease."
notes.11:34: The place name Kibroth-hattaavah (qiḇrōṯ hattaʾăwāh) means "Graves of Craving," playing directly on the verbs "buried" (qāḇərû) and "who had been craving" (hammiṯʾawwîm, Hithpael participle of ʾwh).
notes.12:1: The verb "spoke" (Hebrew Piel 3fs) is feminine singular, agreeing first with Miriam before Aaron is named. The idiom "spoke against" uses the same verb-preposition construction (d-b-r + b) that means "speak through" in v. 2 and "speak with" in vv. 6 and 8.
notes.12:6: Following the Masoretic accents, "the LORD" opens the main clause ("I, the LORD, make Myself known"), though some construe it with the preceding clause as "a prophet of the LORD among you." The verb "make Myself known" is Hithpael of y-d-a.
notes.12:8: "In plain sight" renders the adverbial masculine noun mar'eh (appearance/sight), contrasting with the feminine noun mar'ah (vision) in v. 6.
notes.12:10: The Pual participle rendered "leprous" refers to tzaraat, a biblical scaly skin affliction broader than modern Hansen's disease; the Hebrew text has no separate word for "white" before "like snow."
notes.13:2: The Hebrew verb tur ("scout out") denotes reconnaissance or surveying rather than covert spying. The Hebrew shifts from a singular command addressed to Moses ("Send for yourself") to a plural verb ("you shall send").
notes.13:21: The Hebrew expression lebo chamath can be rendered either directionally as "at the entrance to Hamath" or as the northern border place name Lebo-hamath.
notes.13:22: The Masoretic text shifts from plural "they went up" to singular "he came," often taken distributively or with particular reference to Caleb (cf. Josh 14:12-14), whereas the Septuagint and Samaritan Pentateuch harmonize to the plural.
notes.13:30: "Before Moses" renders el-Mosheh, which can mean "in Moses' presence" or "against/concerning Moses." Both "surely go up" and "can indeed prevail" reflect emphatic Hebrew infinitive absolute constructions.
notes.14:9: Hebrew uses two vivid idioms here: "our bread" means easily consumed or defeated, and "their shade" is a metaphor for their shelter and protection.
notes.14:18: The emphatic Piel infinitive absolute plus imperfect literally reads "acquitting He will not acquit," with "the guilty" implied; the Qal participle rendered "bringing ... to account" denotes judicial reckoning or consequence.
notes.14:21: The Niphal verb takes a definite direct-object marker before "the entire earth" in a passive construction, and the oath formula continues into v. 23, where conditional "if they see" functions idiomatically as an emphatic negative oath.
notes.14:34: "My hostility" translates the rare noun tenuah (occurring elsewhere only in the plural at Job 33:10), derived from a root meaning to frustrate, oppose, or alienate.
notes.14:36: Translated according to the Qere, a Hiphil causative form ("caused ... to grumble") matching the direct object "the whole congregation"; the written Ketiv form is Niphal ("grumbled").
notes.15:4: The Hebrew noun issaron literally means a tenth-part, referring to the standard dry measure equal to one-tenth of an ephah (similarly in 15:6 and 15:9).
notes.15:20: The phrase lift up a contribution translates the Hiphil of rum with its cognate noun terumah (also in 15:19), denoting a portion lifted off and set apart from a larger bulk; dough renders the plural noun arisot (also in 15:21), referring to batches of dough or coarse-ground meal.
notes.15:30: The expression with a high hand translates the Hebrew idiom beyad ramah, denoting deliberate, brazen defiance in contrast to the inadvertent errors of 15:24-29.
notes.15:35: The command shall stone translates the Qal infinitive absolute ragom used with imperative force to issue a solemn order, with the whole congregation as its explicit subject.
notes.15:39: The verb go roving translates the Qal imperfect of tur (to explore, scout, roam), echoing the same verb used repeatedly for scouting the land in Numbers 13-14.
notes.16:1: The Qal verb vayyiqqach ('and he took') lacks an explicit direct object before the conjunction on 'and Dathan'; 'took with him' smooths the elliptical syntax while preserving the singular verb governed by Korah.
notes.16:11: Ketiv/Qere: the Ketiv reads tlwnw (reflecting a Niphal or Qal form), while the Qere reads tallinu (Hiphil imperfect 2mp of lun, 'you grumble', matching the Hiphil participle mallinim in 17:20); the translation follows the Qere.
notes.16:22: Hebrew ha-ish echad uses the interrogative particle with qamets before the initial guttural aleph, framing a rhetorical question ('will one man sin...?').
notes.16:24: Hebrew mishkan ('dwelling') is singular in construct before all three names ('Korah, Dathan, and Abiram'), using the same noun applied to the LORD's tabernacle in 16:9 and 17:28.
notes.16:30: Hebrew beri'ah yivra literally means 'creates a creation'; the noun beri'ah occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and pairs with its cognate verb bara to denote an unprecedented creative act.
notes.17:3: Hebrew ha-chatta'im ha'elleh be-nafshotam literally reads 'these sinners in/against their lives', using the preposition be- of price or cost ('at the cost of their lives'). The noun riqqu'ei ('hammered sheets') occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.17:10: Hebrew herommu is a Niphal imperative 2mp from the geminate root rmm (a by-form of rum, 'be lifted up'), commanding Moses and Aaron to remove themselves from the congregation.
notes.17:20: Hebrew va-hashikkoti is the sole Hiphil occurrence of shakhakh ('subside / abate') in the Hebrew Bible, expressing God's act of quieting the Israelites' grumblings.
notes.17:28: The emphatic repetition ha-qarev ha-qarev ('who draws near, who draws near') reflects the people's terror, and Qal perfect tamnu with ligvoa literally asks 'have we come to an end in perishing?' (i.e., 'are we to perish altogether?').
notes.18:2: The Niphal verb yillawu ("be joined") plays on the tribal name Levi (lewi), a wordplay also echoed in verse 4 (nilwu).
notes.18:8: Hebrew moshchah ("share") is understood either as a measured allotment from a root meaning "measure" or as an entitlement granted by reason of priestly anointing from mashach ("anoint").
notes.18:10: Hebrew beqodesh haqqodashim is translated here with the preposition be- of essence ("as a most holy thing"); some take it locatively as "in a most holy place," referring to the sacred courtyard precinct.
notes.18:12: Hebrew chelev literally means "fat," used idiomatically here and in verses 29, 30, and 32 for the richest or best portion of produce.
notes.18:29: Hebrew miqdesho ("its consecrated part") is a suffixed form of miqdash (elsewhere "sanctuary"), denoting here the sacred portion set apart from the tithe.
notes.19:2: Hebrew parah adummah literally means "red cow"; parah denotes a cow. The Septuagint renders it damalis ("heifer").
notes.19:3: The third-person masculine singular verbs "slaughter" (shachat) here and "burn" (saraf) in verse 5 are used impersonally ("one shall...") because Eleazar oversees the rite ("before him," "in his sight") rather than slaughtering or burning the cow himself.
notes.19:9: Hebrew chattat ("purification offering") is the same noun translated "sin offering" in 18:9; in this chapter it aligns with the privative Hithpael ("purify himself," vv. 12, 13, 20) and Piel ("purify him," v. 19) stems of chata.
notes.19:12: Following the Masoretic cantillation (tipcha on "seventh day"), both "third day" and "seventh day" modify the Hithpael verb "purify himself," consistent with verse 19; alternatively, "on the seventh day" can be grouped with "he will be clean" and "he will not be clean."
notes.19:15: Hebrew tsamid patil literally reads "lid, cord," an appositional idiom for a cover fastened down tightly with a cord.
notes.20:13: The place-name Meribah ("disputing" or "quarreling") plays on the verb rib ("disputed"). The reflexive Niphal of qadash ("showed Himself to be holy") is followed by bam, which can mean either "among them" or "through them."
notes.20:19: The idiom raq ein-davar literally means "only, there is no matter/thing," conveying "nothing more" or "with no trouble," followed by the cohortative e'evorah ("let me pass through").
notes.20:24: Hebrew ammav is plural ("his peoples" or "his kin"), referring to ancestors and relatives in the idiom "gathered to his kin." The phrase "My word" literally translates pi ("My mouth"), denoting divine command.
notes.21:5: The adjective haqqeloqel ("wretched" or "worthless") is a hapax legomenon, a reduplicated form from the root qalal ("to be light, trifling, or contemptible").
notes.21:14: The quotation from the Book of the Wars of the LORD begins abruptly with the direct object marker et before Waheb in Suphah, reflecting a poetic fragment excerpted without its governing verb; Waheb and Suphah are otherwise unknown place names.
notes.21:24: The Masoretic Text reads the adjective az ("strong"); the Septuagint reads the place-name "Jazer."
notes.21:30: Follows the Masoretic vocalization throughout: wanniram is Qal wayyiqtol 1cp of yarah ("shoot") with a 3mp suffix ("we shot them down"), and wannashim is Hiphil wayyiqtol 1cp of shamam ("lay waste"). MT reads the relative pronoun asher ("which") with a Masoretic extraordinary dot over the resh, without which the consonants spell esh ("fire").
notes.21:32: Translates the Qere wayyoresh (Hiphil wayyiqtol 3ms of yarash, "drove out" or "dispossessed"); the Ketiv writes wyyrsh, corresponding to Qal wayyirash ("took possession of").
notes.22:5: Hebrew literally reads "the eye of the land," an idiom for the visible surface of the ground. The Masoretic Text reads "the sons of his people" rather than a specific tribal name.
notes.22:6: The Masoretic Text shifts from first-person singular in "I may prevail" (Qal) to first-person plural in "we strike" (Hiphil), then back to first-person singular in "I drive them out" (Piel).
notes.22:24: The noun rendered "narrow path" (mish'ol) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes a narrow, walled lane between vineyards.
notes.22:32: The rare Qal verb yarat ("is reckless" or "is perverse") occurs only here and in Job 16:11. The Masoretic Text reads "the way" rather than "your way."
notes.22:33: The particle ulay normally means "perhaps," but here functions as a counterfactual negative conditional ("if ... not," equivalent to lule).
notes.23:3: The noun shephi is understood here adverbially as "to a bare height" (cf. Isaiah 41:18; Jeremiah 3:2), though some older traditions interpret it as "alone" or "quietly."
notes.23:10: The Masoretic Text reads the noun "number" (mispar) with "a fourth part" (rova', possibly alluding to one of Israel's four camp divisions); some ancient versions read the verb "who has numbered."
notes.23:15: The Niphal imperfect iqqareh ("am met") has no explicit object in Hebrew, and the repeated adverb koh ("here ... over there") contrasts Balak's position with Balaam's.
notes.23:22: The rare plural noun to'aphoth with re'em ("wild ox") refers to the animal's towering horns or loftiness. The second clause literally reads "like the horns of a wild ox to him" and may also be understood as "Israel has, as it were, the horns of a wild ox."
notes.23:23: The preposition beth ("against") may alternatively be read locatively ("in Jacob ... in Israel"), and the preposition lamed ("of") may also be rendered "to Jacob and to Israel."
notes.24:3: Hebrew beno Beor preserves an archaic construct ending (-o) meaning "son of Beor." The rare passive participle shetum in "with an opened eye" is disputed, understood either as "opened/unsealed" (paralleling "eyes uncovered" in v. 4) or, linking to satam, as "closed."
notes.24:8: The rare noun to'afot denotes heights, eminence, or the towering horns of a wild ox (cf. 23:22). The final clause literally reads "and his arrows he will shatter/strike through," understood either as an instrumental accusative ("strike through with his arrows") or as shattering the adversary's arrows.
notes.24:17: The Qal verb darak literally means "tread" or "march forth," and pa'atey ("temples") is a dual construct meaning the sides of the brow or edges of territory. The Pilpel verb qarqar means "tear down/demolish," while "sons of Sheth" may refer to a Transjordanian nomadic people or, comparing Jer 48:45, "sons of tumult."
notes.24:22: The Piel infinitive construct leba'er ("for burning/consuming") denotes utter devastation (cf. Isa 5:5; 6:13). Hebrew 'ad-mah literally asks "until what?" ("how long?"), introducing the impending capture of Kain by Asshur.
notes.24:23: Hebrew missumo 'El uses the Qal infinitive construct of sum ("set, appoint") with a proleptic third-person suffix anticipating the explicit subject "God," meaning "when God appoints/ordains this."
notes.25:4: The rare Hiphil imperative hoqa' (from yaqa', "be dislocated/wrenched") denotes a public ritual execution, understood as impaling, hanging, or publicly exposing the offenders before the LORD.
notes.25:8: The verse plays on two rare, similar-sounding Hebrew nouns: haqqubbah ("the tent chamber" or vaulted alcove, a hapax legomenon) and qobatah ("her belly/abdomen").
notes.25:11: Hebrew qinna' (Piel) and its cognate noun qin'ah convey ardent covenantal zeal as well as fierce jealousy, repeated across vv. 11 and 13.
notes.25:12: Hebrew beriti shalom places the noun "peace" in apposition to "My covenant" ("My covenant, peace"), the standard Hebrew idiom for expressing "My covenant of peace" when the governing noun already carries a pronominal suffix.
notes.26:2: "Take a head count" translates a Hebrew idiom literally meaning "lift up the head," used for conducting a census.
notes.26:4: The quotation opens elliptically with "From twenty years old and above," resuming the census command of verse 2 without repeating its verb. Because "the sons of Israel" lacks the direct-object marker used with "Moses," it is taken here as the heading for the tribal register starting in verse 5, though the Masoretic accents link it with the preceding clause.
notes.26:9: "The summoned men" translates the qere (read form), a plural construct adjective meaning "summoned ones"; the ketiv (written form) uses the Qal passive participle of the same root with essentially the same sense.
notes.26:10: The Hebrew noun translated "warning sign" literally denotes a "standard," "banner," or "signal pole," used here figuratively for a public warning.
notes.26:55: The Hebrew pairs a passive verb (Niphal of the root meaning "divide" or "apportion") with the direct-object marker before "the land," an impersonal passive construction also seen in verse 60.
notes.26:59: "Who was born to Levi" translates an active Hebrew clause with an unexpressed feminine subject, literally "whom one bore to Levi."
notes.26:61: "Unauthorized fire" translates a Hebrew phrase literally meaning "strange" or "foreign fire," denoting fire not prescribed by the ritual command.
notes.26:62: "Were not registered" translates a rare Hothpaal (passive of Hithpael) form of the verb meaning "register" or "muster."
notes.27:3: The Hebrew plays on the root ya'ad ("appoint/assemble") by pairing the noun "congregation" ('edah, used twice) with the Niphal participle "banded together" (hanno'adim), which is masculine plural to agree with the collective sense of the feminine singular noun.
notes.27:14: "Command" renders Hebrew pi (literally "My mouth"), with the plural verb "you rebelled" addressing both Moses and Aaron. "To sanctify Me" is a declarative Hiphil infinitive of qadash, meaning to treat or uphold God as holy.
notes.27:18: Hebrew ruach ("spirit") lacks the definite article here and denotes spiritual endowment or the Spirit of God equipping Joshua for leadership. Moses is told to lay his singular "hand" on Joshua here, whereas in 27:23 he lays his dual "hands" on him.
notes.27:20: "Some of your dignity" translates partitive min with hod ("splendor, majesty, dignity"), indicating a shared portion of Moses's leadership authority rather than its complete transfer before his death.
notes.28:4: "At twilight" translates the Hebrew dual phrase ben ha'arbayim, literally "between the two evenings," denoting late afternoon or dusk.
notes.28:7: "Pour out" renders the Hiphil infinitive absolute hassekh (from nasakh) used with imperative force alongside its cognate noun nesekh ("drink offering"). "Strong drink" (shekhar) denotes fermented beverage, whereas 28:14 specifies wine (yayin).
notes.28:9: "Tenth-measures" translates Hebrew 'esronim (singular 'issaron in 28:13, 21, 29), a dry measure equal to one-tenth of an ephah (explicitly stated in 28:5).
notes.28:26: "At your Weeks" translates beshavu'otekhem directly without supplying "Feast of," referring to the Festival of Weeks (Shavuot), seven weeks after Passover.
notes.28:31: "Its grain offering" carries a masculine singular suffix (minchato) referring back to the continual offering (hattamid), while "along with their drink offerings" (veniskehem) stands in a trailing position at the end of the Hebrew clause coordinated with the festival offerings to be prepared.
notes.29:1: Hebrew meleket avodah, literally work of labor or service, denotes regular occupational work, in contrast to the total prohibition of any work on the Day of Atonement in 29:7; teruah literally means a loud blast or shout, referring here to sounding trumpets or horns.
notes.29:3: Hebrew 'esronim (singular 'issaron) is a dry measure equal to one-tenth of an ephah (see 28:5, 9).
notes.29:15: The Hebrew doubles issaron distributively to express one-tenth per lamb; the Masoretic text also places one of its fifteen extraordinary scribal dots (puncta extraordinaria) over the waw of the first issaron.
notes.29:31: The Masoretic text preserves subtle variations in the drink-offering suffixes across the days of the festival: plural 'their drink offerings' in 29:19, plural 'its drink offerings' in 29:31, and 'according to their ordinance' in 29:33, rather than standardizing to the singular forms used on the other days.
notes.29:35: Hebrew atseret, derived from a root meaning to restrain or hold back, denotes a solemn closing assembly marking the conclusion of the seven-day festival.
notes.30:1: In Masoretic versification, 30:1 closes the festival-offering instructions of chapters 28-29; in versifications that number this verse 29:40, Hebrew 30:2-17 becomes 30:1-16.
notes.30:3: Hebrew hishava is a Niphal infinitive absolute continuing the finite verb 'vows' (yiddor); lo yachel uses the Hiphil of halal, literally meaning 'he shall not treat as profane' or violate his spoken word.
notes.30:6: The Hiphil verb heni (from nu, to hold back, restrain, or forbid) takes the woman herself as its direct object, whereas hefer (from parar, to nullify, 30:9, 13-16) takes the vow or obligation as its object.
notes.30:7: Hebrew hayo tihyeh le-ish uses the Qal infinitive absolute plus imperfect of hayah with le-ish, literally 'if she indeed becomes a man's,' an idiom for marriage; mivta (occurring only here and in 30:9) derives from bata, meaning to speak hastily or rashly.
notes.30:14: Hebrew le-annot nefesh (Piel infinitive construct of anah plus nefesh, literally 'to afflict a soul') refers to self-denial such as fasting, matching the same idiom in 29:7; the husband's authority to 'uphold' (Hiphil of qum) corresponds to the Qal 'stand' used earlier for valid vows.
notes.31:5: Hebrew vayyimmasru (Niphal of masar), a rare verb occurring in Biblical Hebrew only here ("were supplied/delivered") and in v. 16 (Qal infinitive construct limsor-ma'al, "to commit unfaithfulness").
notes.31:20: Hebrew titchatta'u (Hithpael imperfect 2mp of chata', normally reflexive "purify yourselves" as in v. 19) here governs fronted objects, indicating that they are to purify those items for themselves.
notes.31:23: Hebrew mey niddah literally means "water of impurity" (or "separation"), referring to the ritual water prepared with the ashes of the red heifer for removing corpse-impurity (Numbers 19:9).
notes.31:30: Hebrew achuz (Qal passive participle of achaz, "grasp/take"; also with the definite article in v. 47) denotes a share drawn or selected out of a larger group.
notes.31:50: Hebrew kumaz occurs only here and in Exodus 35:22; its exact design is uncertain, likely referring to globular gold beads or a beaded necklace.
notes.32:7: Ketiv writes a consonantal waw where Qere reads teni'un, the Hiphil imperfect 2nd person masculine plural with paragogic nun of the root nw' ('turn away, discourage'), matching the Hiphil verb in 32:9.
notes.32:11: Hebrew 'im introducing an oath expresses an emphatic negation ('Surely ... shall not'). The idiom 'follow wholeheartedly' renders the Piel of ml' ('fill, fulfill') followed by 'aharay ('after Me'), echoed in 32:12.
notes.32:14: The Hebrew noun tarbut ('breed, brood, offspring,' derived from rbh, 'increase, multiply') is a hapax legomenon, occurring only here in the Hebrew Bible.
notes.32:19: Hebrew me'ever ('across, on the side of') is used twice in this verse for opposite sides of the Jordan, disambiguated first for the west ('and onward') and then for the east ('toward the east').
notes.32:38: The aside 'with their names changed' translates musabbot shem, a Hophal feminine plural participle of sbb ('turn, change') modifying Nebo and Baal-meon. The final clause literally reads 'and they called by names the names of the cities that they built.'
notes.33:4: Hebrew uses the Piel participle of qabar ('bury'), expressing the extensive burial of many dead across Egypt.
notes.33:8: The Hebrew reads 'from before Hahiroth' (mippenei hahirot), without the 'Pi-' of 33:7.
notes.33:10: Hebrew yam-suph literally means 'Sea of Reeds,' the Septuagint calls it the Red Sea.
notes.33:53: The Hiphil of yarash means 'drive out' when taking inhabitants as its object (33:52, 55), but 'take possession of' when taking the land itself as its object here, paralleling the Qal infinitive 'to possess' at the end of the verse.
notes.33:55: Hebrew sikkim ('barbs') is a biblical hapax legomenon denoting sharp thorns or barbs, paired with tseninim ('thorns'); the verb tsarar ('harass') conveys active hostility.
notes.34:4: Ketiv reads singular והיה ("shall be"), while Qere reads plural וְהָיוּ agreeing with the plural subject תּוֹצְאֹתָיו ("its outer limits," literally "its outgoings").
notes.34:6: MT reads literally הַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל וּגְבוּל ("the Great Sea and a boundary"), referring either to the Mediterranean Sea and its coastal border or using the conjunction epexegetically ("the Great Sea as a boundary").
notes.34:8: לְבֹא חֲמָת is translated as the northern place name Lebo-hamath; it can also be rendered literally as "the entrance of Hamath."
notes.34:17: Here and in v. 18 the Qal of נחל (יִנְחֲלוּ, לִנְחֹל) carries the transitive sense "apportion as an inheritance" (parallel to the Piel לְנַחֵל in v. 29), whereas v. 13 uses the Hithpael (תִּתְנַחֲלוּ) for "inherit for yourselves."
notes.35:6: Hebrew uses the single root רצח (רֹצֵחַ) throughout this chapter both for an accidental or untried killer (vv. 6, 11-12, 25-28) and for a culpable murderer under capital sentence (vv. 16-19, 21, 30-31), as well as for lawful execution by the avenger of blood (vv. 27, 30).
notes.35:11: וְהִקְרִיתֶם is the Hiphil of קרה ("cause to meet" or "make accessible"), used here for designating conveniently located cities of refuge.
notes.35:25: Hebrew expresses "who was anointed" via an active impersonal construction (אֲשֶׁר־מָשַׁח אֹתוֹ, literally "whom one anointed"); a similar indefinite active construction appears in v. 30 (יִרְצַח אֶת־הָרֹצֵחַ, literally "one shall kill the murderer").
notes.35:32: MT vocalizes לָנוּס as the Qal infinitive construct ("for fleeing"), understood here substantivally as "for one who has fled," and reads simply הַכֹּהֵן ("the priest") without "high" (contrast vv. 25, 28).
notes.36:2: Hebrew pairs the active Piel in the first clause ("the LORD commanded my lord") with the passive Pual in the second ("my lord was commanded by the LORD"), using the preposition be- ("by") to mark the divine agent of the passive verb.
notes.36:3: The opening conditional ("Now if they become...") renders a paratactic Hebrew weqatal sequence. After the feminine singular Niphal verb agreeing with "their inheritance," the verse shifts to masculine singular Niphal forms ("will be added" and "will be deducted") used impersonally of the transferred portion.
notes.36:6: The pronouns in "their eyes" and "their father" use masculine plural suffixes in Hebrew even though they refer to Zelophehad's daughters, in contrast to the feminine plural suffixes used in verses 3, 4, 11, and 12.
notes.36:12: Hebrew reverses the construct order found in verses 6 and 8 ("the clan of their/her father's tribe"), reading literally "the tribe of their father's clan."
notes.36:13: Hebrew literally reads "beside the Jordan of Jericho," a construct phrase used repeatedly in Numbers to designate the stretch of the Jordan River adjacent to Jericho.

unplaced.text: And it happened after the plague,
unplaced.note: In the Hebrew text this clause forms its own verse, 25:19, which leads into the census of chapter 26.
